newsitem.title: INDIA: Storm veers away from India, may hit Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Storm veers away from India, may hit Bangladesh.

text.p: A cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal that threatened to lash southeastern India appeared on Saturday to veer away and head towards Bangladesh, local officials said.
Earlier, thousands of people began to evacuate Andhra Pradesh as their second cyclone in three weeks seemed imminent.
Officials said the depression in the Bay of Bengal had changed course and appeared to be heading northeast towards Bangladesh.
"We are a bit relaxed since the cyclonic threat has receded," Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said.
Naidu, quoting meteorological officials, told reporters the depression was likely to miss Andhra Pradesh but said authorities would continue to watch coastal districts.
He said the depression was 450 km (280 miles) off Andhra Pradesh at 6.30 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Saturday.
State Relief Commissioner H.S. Brahma earlier said officials in nine coastal areas of fishing villages and rice and oilseed farms had been asked to help in the evacuation.

A total of 971 people were killed and 925 were missing after a cyclone hit the coast on November 7. More than 177,000 people were evacuated from the worst affected areas, which suffered an estimated $1.4 billion worth of damage.
The United News of India quoted Andhra Pradesh Revenue Minister Devender Goud on Friday as saying state authorities had asked the army, navy and air force to help the evacuation.
Officials on the coast hoisted danger signals and urged fishermen not to put out to sea. The navy and coastguard were asked to warn fishermen at sea to return home.
